correctness.rationale: Eliminating the hub using the zero-sum condition gives the negative distance quadratic form from the anchored matrix with entries d(o,i)^p+d(o,j)^p-d(i,j)^p. Its two arm-coordinate subspaces split into constant and mean-zero vectors. With x=2^p, y=3^p and t=sqrt(x), the fluctuation block is (x,y-1;y-1,x^2), positive definite for 0<p<2 since y-1<t^3 by strict subadditivity of the p/2 power. The constant block is (A,C0;C0,xA), A=2q-(q-1)x, C0=q(1+x)-1-(q-1)y. Its factors are F=tA+C0 and G=tA-C0. Independent sign checks give F(1)=2+2 sqrt(2), F'<0 for p>=1 and F(p_A)<0: 2*3^p-4^p-2 is strictly concave on [1,2] and vanishes at its endpoints. For 1<p<2 and F>=0, the real arm count lies between 0 and the root count Q(p), below the count x/(x-2) at which A vanishes; G is affine in the count, positive at 0 by subadditivity and at Q(p) because it equals 2tA there. Thus only one radial direction becomes null, namely (t,1); for all p above the root its quadratic form in the constant block is 2tF<0. Strictness below 1 follows from Li–Weston (or the p=0 matrix directly there). Centering gives affine ranks 2q and 2q-1, and q=2 is a path whose endpoint 2 follows from its line embedding and the three-point second-difference witness above 2. The root decreases in q since 3^p+t^3>(1+t)^2 for p>1. Differentiation at (p,1/q)=(1,0) gives the stated C=1.2476366340867857. The frozen numerical checker is corroboration, not the basis for the universal sign or rank claims.
